1.w: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, the one having met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and having blessed him,

2.w: to whom also Abraham apportioned a tenth of all, first indeed being translated, “king of righteousness;” and then also, “king of Salem,” which is, “king of peace,”

3.w: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but having been made like the Son of God, remains a priest in perpetuity.

4.w: Now behold how great this one [was], to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth out of the best spoils.

5.w: And indeed, those out from the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood have a commandment to take a tenth from the people, according to the law—that is, from their brothers, though having come forth out of the loin of Abraham.

6.w: But the one not tracing his descent out from them has collected a tenth from Abraham and has blessed the one having the promises.

7.w: And apart from all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

8.w: And here indeed, dying men receive the tenths; but there, it is being testified that he lives.

9.w: and so to say a word, even Levi, the one receiving the tenths, has paid the tenth through Abraham.

10.w: For he was still in the loin of [his] father when Melchizedek met him.

11.w: Then indeed, if perfection were by the Levitical priesthood (for upon it the people had received the law) what need [was] still [for] another priest to arise, according to the order of Melchizedek and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?

12.w: For the priesthood being changed, out of necessity a change of law also takes place.

13.w: For [he] of whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, from which no one has attended at the altar.

14.w: For [it is] evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, a tribe in regard to which Moses spoke nothing about priests.

15.w: And it is yet more abundantly evident if another priest according to the likeness of Melchizedek arises,

16.w: who has become [such] not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.

17.w: For it is testified: “You [are] a priest to the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

18.w: For indeed, there is a putting away of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness

19.w: (for the law perfected nothing), and the introduction of a better hope, by which we draw near to God.

20.w: And inasmuch as [it was] not without an oath (for those indeed apart from an oath are become priests),

21.w: the One, however, [was] with an oath through the One saying to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind; ‘You [are] a priest to the age.’”

22.w: By so much also, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

23.w: And indeed those having become priests are many, because of by death being prevented from continuing.

24.w: But because of His remaining to the age, He has the permanent priesthood,

25.w: wherefore also He is able to save to the uttermost those drawing near to God through Him, always living to intercede for them.

26.w: For such for us indeed was fitting—a high priest holy, innocent, undefiled, having been separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens,

27.w: who has no need every day, as the first high priests, to offer up sacrifices for [his] own sins, then for those of the people; for He did this once for all, having offered up Himself.

28.w: For the law appoints as high priests men having weakness; but the word of the oath, which [is] after the law, [appoints] a Son having been perfected to the age.
